newsitem.title: GERMANY: German union repeats record Jan jobless forecast.
newsitem.headline: German union repeats record Jan jobless forecast.

text.p: The deputy head of Germany's DGB Trade Union Federation on Friday repeated that she expected the country's January jobless total to exceed 4.4 million marks, a sharp rise from December's 4.15 million and a post-World War Two record.
"Our estimates indicate that the number of registered unemployed will be 4.4 million this month, and that is a record after World War Two," Ursula Engelen-Kefer told Reuters Financial Television.

Engelen-Kefer, who sits on the board of the German Labour Office that publishes monthly unemployment data, also criticised Germany's recent tax reform plans, saying they penalised low-income workers and benefited the wealthy.
"In the end, it is these (low) income groups who would have higher taxes," she said.

Noting that German unions could only strike in the context of collective wage bargaining, Engelen-Kefer said the unions still planned other forms of protest and hoped to stop the tax legislation from passing parliament.
"We hope we can stop this so-called reform by legislative measures," she said.
The government should seek alternative ways to meet Maastricht Treaty terms rather than adding to the unemployment problem, she said.

"We have made concrete proposals. We need more redistribution of work, reduction of overtime... The Maastricht criteria are flexible, and the government does not have to use unjust proposals to meet them," Engelen-Kefer said.
